question.problem:
Let $X$ be a continuous random variable with the following probability density function:

$$
{f}_{X}(x)=\{\begin{aligned}{e}^{2-x}, & x\ge 2 \\ 0, & \text{otherwise}\end{aligned}
$$

If the probability density function of $Y=(X-4)^{2}$ is given by 

$$
{f}_{Y}(y)=\{\begin{aligned}g(y), & 0<y<4 \\ h(y), & y\ge 4 \\ 0, & \text{otherwise}\end{aligned}
$$

find the function $g(y).$

current_example.worked_solution:
First, let's visualize the transformation $Y = X^2$ over the interval $-1 <            x <         2.$

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/differential/14231916/assets/c98b2d947486e4666380dc8412c1b64a8518c84e39372052602a9402ab3d4211.png)

Notice the following:

- The transformation is two-to-one over the interval $-1 \lt   x <       1.$ On this interval, $Y$ is nonzero on $0 \lt  y \lt 1.$

- The transformation is one-to-one over the interval $1 \leq x \lt  2.$ On this interval, $Y$ is nonzero on $1 \leq  y \lt   4.$

In this question, we're asked to consider only the interval $1 \leq  y \lt   4.$

Using the definition of the cumulative distribution of $Y,$ for $1 \leq  y \lt   4,$ we have

$$
\begin{aligned}{F}_{Y}(y) & =P(Y\le y) \\  & =P({X}^{2}\le y) \\  & =P(\sqrt{{X}^{2}}\le \sqrt{y}) \\  & =P(|X|\le \sqrt{y}) \\  & =P(X\le \sqrt{y}) \\  & ={F}_{X}(\sqrt{y}).\end{aligned}
$$

Notice that we used $|X| = X$ for $X > 0.$

To compute the PDF $f_Y(y)$ for $1 \leq  y \lt   4,$ we differentiate $F_Y$ with respect to $y$ using the chain rule. This gives

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}_{Y}(y) & ={F}_{Y}^{′}(y) \\  & =\frac{1}{2\sqrt{y}}\cdot {F}_{X}^{′}(\sqrt{y}) \\  & =\frac{1}{2\sqrt{y}}\cdot {f}_{X}(\sqrt{y}).\end{aligned}
$$

Applying the definition of $f_X,$ we finally arrive at

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}_{Y}(y) & =\frac{1}{2\sqrt{y}}\cdot {f}_{X}(\sqrt{y}) \\  & =\frac{1}{2\sqrt{y}}\cdot \frac{5}{33}(\sqrt{y})^{4} \\  & =\frac{1}{2\sqrt{y}}\cdot \frac{5}{33}{y}^{2} \\  & =\frac{5}{66}\,{y}^{3/2}.\end{aligned}
$$

Consequently, $h(y) = \dfrac{5}{66}\,y^{3/2}.$
